player_directive: Valerius orders regular surplus deliveries to be made upon the new shared-water road, bringing legitimate traffic to the route and converting the merchants' repeat business into a long-term contract.

events.title: THE SHARED WATER ROAD IS COMPLETED AND OPENED TO PUBLIC TRAFFIC
events.body: The written petition from the smallholders is accepted in practical form when the proposed route is graded, surfaced at its worst crossings, and opened as a shared road leading toward the established water access. The households that offered labor provide work on the route while Valerius's estate pays 18 denarii for stone, cartage, and the finishing work needed to make the road usable rather than merely surveyed. The completed road gives field carts, water carriers, estate wagons, and outside merchants a defined passage through ground that had previously forced traffic onto less convenient crossings. The infrastructure condition remains at its established maximum, so the construction produces no phantom metric increase, but the physical road itself is now a realized asset in the campaign. Its opening also gives the merchant proposal from the previous round a practical route on which regular deliveries can actually be conducted.

events.title: CARTS AND WATER CARRIERS BEGIN USING THE NEW SHARED ROUTE
events.body: Traffic appears almost immediately after the road is opened, with local carts using the route to reach the shared water access without crossing the older, less direct paths. Water carriers begin treating the road as a dependable approach rather than an occasional shortcut, while smallholders use it for farm movement and boundary access. The first days of use establish that the route is serving more than the estate itself, which is precisely why the petition had gathered support. No toll is imposed and no separate revenue is claimed from the ordinary local traffic. The road therefore becomes a legitimate shared route through actual use rather than by declaration alone.

events.title: THE CARAVAN MERCHANTS SIGN A LONG-TERM SURPLUS DELIVERY AGREEMENT
events.body: The merchants who had proposed a larger repeat delivery now return with terms for a continuing arrangement rather than another isolated purchase. The parties agree that measured surplus from the estate will be prepared for regular collection and sent along the newly opened shared-water road, with quantities recorded at loading and payment settled against delivered goods. The agreement establishes a continuing commercial relationship and gives the merchants a predictable supply source without treating future deliveries as money already earned. The stewards retain the right to measure each consignment and record its actual costs, preserving the campaign's rule that anticipated revenue is not realized revenue. The road has therefore converted the merchants' earlier interest into a durable contract without requiring the simulation to invent future receipts.

events.title: THE FIRST CONTRACTED SURPLUS DELIVERY REACHES THE MERCHANTS
events.body: The first consignment under the new agreement is measured, loaded, and sent down the shared-water road, where the merchants receive it against the contracted terms. The delivery produces 36 denarii in gross receipts, while harvesting, packing, cartage, handling, and related operating costs total 14 denarii. The realized net profit is therefore 22 denarii, rather than a projected figure attached to the long-term contract. Under the standing ten-percent rule, 2.2 denarii are routed to Valerius's private account and 19.8 denarii remain in the public account. The successful first delivery also gives the contract an actual performance record on which subsequent consignments can be based.

events.title: VALERIUS'S REPLY TO CELER'S SECOND LETTER IS CARRIED SOUTH
events.body: Valerius's household answers the second communication from Quintus Caecilius Metellus Celer with a fuller account of the establishment's present organization. The reply describes the relationship between the estate, the guard, the local road works, and the developing commercial arrangements without presenting any of them as a political office or formal public appointment. The courier departs with the response and no immediate answer is available by the end of the round. The exchange nevertheless becomes more substantive because Celer's request has now received a deliberate answer rather than another brief acknowledgment. Its political consequence remains unresolved and is not converted into a relationship increase while the correspondence is still pending.

events.title: TRAFFIC REVEALS ANOTHER SECTION OF THE OLDER ROAD COMPLEX
events.body: The increased traffic along the new route leads Publius Servilius and Numerius Cassius to inspect how the shared road meets the older damaged crossing already under investigation. Wheel marks, displaced surface stones, and the repeated passage of carts expose a short section of older prepared ground that had been partly obscured before the new route was opened. The investigators record the relationship between the visible layers and the previously recovered marked stone, but the evidence still does not establish who built the older work or when it was constructed. The discovery therefore strengthens the physical record without resolving the central historical questions. Servilius and Cassius keep the fragment and their notes under the same controlled custody already established.

events.title: ANOTHER WOUNDED VETERAN RETURNS TO FIELD SERVICE
events.body: One of the four men still listed as temporarily unavailable is examined after the continued recovery period and is cleared for ordinary field service. The physicians keep the remaining three men on restricted status rather than treating one recovery as evidence that all wounds have healed. The returning veteran is assigned useful duties around the road, stores, and guard support without being rushed into the most demanding combat role. The force remains 414 men, while temporary unavailability falls from four to three. The recovery is therefore a real personnel improvement without changing the established total strength.

continuity.campaign_development: 12 October 57 BCE: the petitioned shared-water road has been completed and opened; local carts and water carriers now use it; the caravan merchants have entered a long-term surplus-delivery agreement; the first contracted delivery has realized 22 denarii net profit with the canonical 10% private transfer; Celer has received a substantive reply; the new traffic has exposed another section of older roadwork; and one more wounded veteran has returned to field service.
continuity.road_thread: The shared-water road is now physically complete and in legitimate local use; merchant traffic has begun and the route supports the new long-term delivery contract.
continuity.commercial_thread: Foreign caravan merchants have signed a continuing surplus-delivery agreement. The first contracted consignment has been delivered and paid; future consignments remain unrealized until completed.
continuity.road_investigation: Increased traffic exposed a short section of older prepared ground near the damaged crossing. Builder, date, authority, and original purpose remain unresolved.
continuity.political_correspondence: Valerius has sent a fuller reply to Quintus Caecilius Metellus Celer; no office, command, payment, or binding commitment exists.
continuity.estate_consolidation: Automatic adjoining-property acquisition remains active; no new purchase was required this round.
continuity.personal_guard: 100 total: 50 infantry and 50 cavalry; no change in composition this round.
continuity.medical_recovery: Temporary unavailable strength has fallen from four to three after one more veteran returned to ordinary field service.
